title: test(lint): index the access-matrix rows once in the exhaustive fold case
body:
Part of #22346

Clause-②: no

## What changed

One test case, test-only: `packages/lint/src/build-access-matrix.test.ts`, "exhaustively matches the fold over every declared bit combination". Its per-entry `m.entries.find(...)` lookup is replaced by one `Map`, built once from `m.entries` and keyed by `permissionSet`. The first match wins, so every lookup returns the same row `find` returned. The 3^8 enumeration, the cell count and all four assertions are unchanged. `build-access-matrix.ts` is untouched, no timeout is raised, and nothing is skipped.

Why `Part of`: the card's generator closes the card when an hourly run is green. Its second cause, the shard-timing drift, belongs to #22014, which remains open. This PR removes only the lint case's half.

## Measurements

All wall times were taken under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` in a shared container. The lock excludes other locked runs, not unlocked sibling work, so the ratios carry more weight than the absolute numbers.

**H1: the lookup is quadratic (confirmed).** A counter in the `find` callback, written the same way as the case, read 21,526,641 calls per run. That is 6,561 × 6,562 / 2, and each call rebuilds the `ps_NNNN` name.

**H2: the lookup dominates (confirmed).** A scratch script (not committed) timed each step of the case three times at `54c3ce10c`:

| step | iter 1 | iter 2 | iter 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| enumerate the 3^8 entries | 4.5 ms | 1.0 ms | 0.9 ms |
| map entries to permission sets | 1.6 ms | 1.9 ms | 0.6 ms |
| `buildAccessMatrix` | 25.0 ms | 14.7 ms | 3.1 ms |
| lookup, per-entry `find` (as on main) | 950.8 ms | 779.8 ms | 845.7 ms |
| lookup, `Map` built once | 2.7 ms | 1.3 ms | 1.7 ms |
| fold comparison loop | 5.6 ms | 1.7 ms | 1.7 ms |

No other step in the case is quadratic. `buildAccessMatrix`, its sort included, costs too little to report.

**Case wall time**, as vitest reports it per test. Command: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 --reporter=verbose src/build-access-matrix.test.ts`, three runs per tree:

| tree | run 1 | run 2 | run 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| before, `54c3ce10c` | 700 ms | 613 ms | 751 ms |
| after, `b447bfa07` | 46 ms | 44 ms | 47 ms |

That is about 15x faster. CI crossed the 5 s default only on a loaded shard (the triage measured a 473 s import phase there). At this container's speed, the case now runs at about 1/100 of the limit.

**Ablation.** `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` put the per-entry `find` back in place of the `Map` lookup three times, each in wrap mode. Each time the anchor count went 1 → 0, the replacement count went 0 → 1, and the blob went `84866b0a6a8f` → `40761cc2c49a`.

| leg | run 1 | run 2 | run 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `find` put back (mutation) | 834 ms | 803 ms | 696 ms |

All 8 cases passed under the mutation, which is expected: the timing is the pin, and no assertion was added. On every restore leg, the blob after restore equalled the blob at HEAD (`84866b0a6a8f`), and `git diff HEAD` was empty.

## The assertions are unchanged

The case has 4 `expect(` calls before and after the change. Their matcher text is identical (compared as text with `cmp`):

```
expect(entries.length).toBe(3 ** 8)
expect(m.entries.length).toBe(entries.length)
expect(cells).toBe(3 ** 8 * 4)
expect(mismatches).toEqual([])
```

Across the whole file there are 28 `expect(` lines before and after, byte-identical as a sorted set, and 8 `it(` cases before and after. The full diff of the case:

```diff
     expect(m.entries.length).toBe(entries.length);
+    // Index the rows by permission set ONCE. A `find` per entry is quadratic —
+    // 3^8 entries make ~21.5M callbacks, each rebuilding the name — which ran
+    // this case past vitest's 5 s default on a loaded CI shard. First match
+    // wins, so every lookup returns the row `find` returned.
+    const rowByPermissionSet = new Map TYPE_ARGS ();
+    for (const e of m.entries) {
+      if (!rowByPermissionSet.has(e.permissionSet)) rowByPermissionSet.set(e.permissionSet, e);
+    }
     const mismatches: string[] = [];
     let cells = 0;
     for (let i = 0; i LESS_THAN entries.length; i++) {
-      const row = m.entries.find((e) => e.permissionSet === `ps_${String(i).padStart(4, '0')}`)!;
+      const row = rowByPermissionSet.get(`ps_${String(i).padStart(4, '0')}`)!;
```

Two placeholders stand in for angle-bracket text, which GitHub's body sanitizer removes. `TYPE_ARGS` is the Map's two type arguments: `string`, and the entry type written as `(typeof m.entries)[number]`. `LESS_THAN` is the less-than operator. The committed lines are in the file.

  - Population: the diff's only path. `--print-config` shows that ESLint lints it, with 5 rules.
  - Invariance: the config enables no type-aware linting for this file (`parserOptions.project` and `projectService` are both null), and the diff edits no config. So no untouched file's verdict can change.

  - 52 ran green on the first pass.
  - `check:lean-entry-closure` first refused with PREREQUISITE NOT MET. It is green after building the `@objectstack/objectql` closure.
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` refused with PREREQUISITE NOT MET because it needs every package built. It is NOT MEASURED locally and is left to CI.
  - `--ran` verdict: "54 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 53 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED (1 DERIVED from a recorded exit 3)".

- The diff is test-only. Under AGENTS.md, the label is for a diff that publishes nothing from any released package.
- Measured after `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint build`: the package's `files` are `dist`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`. The new symbol `rowByPermissionSet` and the case title have 0 hits there; the positive control `buildAccessMatrix` has 6.
